dedupe_keys.name: social ecological database for research on infrastructure development impacts in the brazilian amazon

description: This database brings together multiple datasets from human health, socio-economics, environment, hydrology and energy to give a baseline for studying the long-term effects of infrastructure development in the Brazilian Amazon. It includes point data on river water level, discharge and daily precipitation for the Amazon, Tocantins-Araguaia, Paraná and Atlantic watersheds; disease incidence by municipality for malaria, dengue, cutaneous leishmaniasis and HIV/AIDS; municipal environmental variables such as rainfall, dry season length, original forest cover and surface water; socio-economic variables on demography, education, income, work, agriculture, poverty and gold mining; a table of operating large hydroelectric dams over 30 MW with river, construction, reservoir fill and operation dates, approved and actual energy output, reservoir area and flooded area per affected municipality; and 2010 municipal boundary maps. It was compiled by Joanna Tucker Lima, Denis Valle and colleagues at the University of Florida and the Universidade de São Paulo, described in Scientific Data in 2016, and is downloadable from Dryad (about 348 MB, CSV, ZIP and shapefiles) under CC0. Caveats: coverage years differ by theme, and it was not updated after 2017. It supports hazard exposure and resilience studies of hydropower and water infrastructure and their social impacts; a related record is the Global Flood Database.
